Daily Brief

Thursday's news is dominated by the aftermath of Spain's deadly train crash, which killed at least 68 people and has prompted three days of national mourning [BBC, RFI, Le Monde, The Hindu]. Audio recordings suggest the collision resulted from a control centre error after a computer failure halted trains on the Madrid-Seville line. In Israel, partial election results show Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc leading but short of a majority, with Arab-led parties securing a historic 19 seats and potentially holding kingmaker status [BBC, Al Jazeera, ABC Australia]. The election's aftermath has been marred by Netanyahu's allegations that Arab parties 'stole' the vote, prompting demands for a foreign interference probe. ECB President Christine Lagarde announced she will resign in February 2027, nine months early, amid speculation the move is designed to allow EU leaders to select her successor before France's presidential election [Le Monde, The Hindu]. A ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV has been extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, offering hope for humanitarian aid deliveries to trapped civilians [BBC]. Meanwhile, with US midterm elections five days away, both President Trump and former President Obama are making closing appeals in battleground states [Globe and Mail].

01 Conflict

Spain Train Crash Kills at Least 68; Audio Reveals Control Centre Error

  • A high-speed Renfe train collided with a stationary Iryo train on the Madrid-Seville line Wednesday morning, killing at least 68 people and injuring over 100
  • Audio recordings indicate a computer failure forced trains to halt, but the control centre then gave the Renfe train clearance to proceed 'in error' while the Iryo train remained stopped 25km ahead
  • Spain has declared three days of national mourning; Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez visited the crash site and vowed a full investigation
  • This is the second fatal high-speed rail accident in Spain in 2026, raising questions about railway safety systems

02 Geopolitics

Israel Election Deadlocked as Arab Parties Win Historic 19 Seats

  • With 93% of votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc leads with 53 projected seats while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc has 48, both short of the 61-seat majority needed
  • Arab-led parties secured an unprecedented 19 seats driven by approximately 80% turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel
  • Netanyahu claimed the election was 'stolen by Arab parties'; the Central Elections Committee head has demanded a Shin Bet investigation into foreign interference allegations
  • Coalition negotiations could take weeks, with the possibility of another election if no government can be formed

03 Economics

ECB President Lagarde to Resign Early in February 2027

  • Christine Lagarde announced she will leave the ECB presidency on February 7, 2027, nine months before her eight-year term was scheduled to end
  • The early departure is widely seen as allowing EU leaders to select a successor while French President Macron remains in office, before France's presidential election
  • Two other senior ECB positions are also becoming vacant: chief economist Philip Lane's term ends May 31 and board member Isabel Schnabel is leaving for the IMF
  • European Council President Antonio Costa said the selection process would begin immediately

Ceasefire Extended Across Ukraine's Kherson Region for Humanitarian Access

  • A ceasefire initially focused on the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has been expanded to cover the entire Kherson region in southern Ukraine
  • US First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV helped broker the deal to allow food and medicine deliveries to thousands of trapped civilians
  • Humanitarian aid deliveries to Oleshky are planned, followed by evacuations on Friday for those wishing to leave
  • Both Russian and Ukrainian officials confirmed the ceasefire was being observed with no reported breaches
